findings.claim: A new job starts with no associated processes. AssignProcessToJobObject associates a process; default CreateProcess children created after association join the job.
findings.requirements: Association must be established for job-based cleanup of a child; this source explicitly describes children created after association.
findings.exceptions: WMI Win32_Process.Create is excluded in this overview. Breakaway flags and parent nested-job settings can change association.
findings.engineering_inference: To promise cleanup of application-created descendants, establish and verify membership before permitting application work that could create them. The source does not choose how a launcher enforces that ordering.

findings.claim: With JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE set, closing the last job handle terminates associated processes; for a nested job it also covers associated child-job processes.
findings.requirements: The documented condition is last job-object handle closure, not direct-child exit, one arbitrary CloseHandle, or launcher control-signal delivery.
findings.engineering_inference: Ownership and inheritance of every relevant job handle matter to cleanup correctness; preventing unintended additional handles must be proved by the implementation.
findings.limits: The selected overview establishes semantics, not numeric flag value, ctypes field layout, binding correctness or a completion-wait implementation.

findings.claim: TerminateJobObject is the documented operation for all currently associated job processes. CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP instead supports console CTRL+BREAK delivery.
findings.applicability: Job-wide cleanup and console notification are distinct documented operations.
findings.limits: The creation-flags source supplies no guarantee that CTRL+BREAK recipients exit. These selected bodies do not establish detailed TerminateJobObject return, wait or exception semantics; root separately verified its exact API page.

findings.claim: Assignment requires JOB_OBJECT_ASSIGN_PROCESS on the job handle and PROCESS_SET_QUOTA plus PROCESS_TERMINATE on the process handle. Zero indicates failure, with GetLastError for details.
findings.exceptions: Some limit failures terminate the supplied process, while other documented restrictions simply make assignment fail. A terminating job or parent also causes failure.
findings.engineering_inference: Do not release application startup after an assignment error or assume every assignment failure cleaned up the created process. Cleanup and failure preservation are explicit engineering obligations.

findings.claim: Existing job membership has nested-job/UI-limit/session constraints; multiple job association began in Windows8/Server2012.
findings.exceptions: Older Windows single-job behavior, compatibility jobs, allowed breakaway and nested-parent limits can affect assignment/descendant containment. The old-version process-tree alternatives in the overview are not a general recommendation to allow breakaway.
findings.engineering_inference: A nested-job failure must remain visible; weakening breakaway limits to make a check pass changes the promised containment and cannot be inferred as authorized.

findings.claim: CREATE_SUSPENDED (0x00000004) creates the primary thread suspended; that thread does not run until ResumeThread is called.
findings.requirements: The guaranteed scope is the primary thread. A separate AssignProcessToJobObject security-token exception requires suspended creation, but this is not a documented requirement that every possible job assignment use it.
findings.limits: No source proves equivalence with a Python stdin gate, Python startup side-effect freedom, private Popen thread-handle access or recovery of a thread handle already closed by Python.

findings.claim: CreateProcess returns process and primary-thread handles that remain valid until closed, even after termination; the documented process-identifier validity lasts from creation until termination.
findings.requirements: Retained native handle lifetime and numeric PID lifetime are distinct. OpenProcess accepts a PID and explicit rights/inheritance.
findings.engineering_inference: Do not treat a saved numeric PID after termination as stable ownership evidence or reacquire it to represent the same created child. Retaining the original handle avoids relying on a stronger PID lifetime guarantee than this text provides.
findings.limits: The source does not specify the exact PID-reuse timing nor the Python representation/ownership/closing behavior of process handles.

findings.claim: Selected official Win32 bodies do not establish the Python startup architecture or every binding detail.
topics: Cooperative stdin gate correctness and EOF/parent-death behavior
Safety of imports or startup before a gate under Python -I -B -S
CPython subprocess private handles and thread-handle closure
Exact JOBOBJECT_EXTENDED_LIMIT_INFORMATION ABI and numeric kill-on-close/info-class constants
Retroactive capture of descendants that existed before assignment
Native Windows behavior/parity on the actual packaged application
findings.resolution: Root engineering contract, separate API/ABI verification and meaningful native/portable checks decide these. Absence of source proof is neither architecture selection nor evidence that an approach cannot work.

findings.claim: Generated answer says suspended creation is necessary for a generic launcher and is the only native way to guarantee startup ordering.
findings.reason: The selected texts define CREATE_SUSPENDED primary-thread behavior and one security-token requirement. They do not compare every startup mechanism or establish necessity/uniqueness for the root contract. The generated answer itself separately recognizes that cooperative Python gating is not evaluated.
findings.resolution: Do not adopt the necessity/uniqueness claim or infer rejection/acceptance of the proposed gate.

findings.claim: Generated diagram asserts instant PID invalidation/recycling and links a retained process handle to QueryInformationJobObject accuracy.
findings.reason: The selected handle text specifies handle validity until closed and PID validity until termination; it does not establish precise recycling timing. QueryInformationJobObject is a job-object API, so that example is not established by a retained process-handle passage.
findings.resolution: Use only the exact documented lifetime distinction, and keep numeric PID reuse timing and unrelated API guarantees out of implementation authority.

findings.claim: Generated answer generalizes the old single-job process-tree paragraph into universal failure of every subsequent child job association when breakaway is prohibited.
findings.reason: The overview alternatives are explicitly for cases where nested jobs cannot be used, while the assignment page separately documents modern nested-job association. Neither universal failure nor guaranteed nesting success follows.
findings.resolution: Preserve actual nested-job, UI/session and parent-limit constraints and fail visibly on concrete assignment errors.

findings.claim: Generated language about atomic or immediate subtree destruction and standard single-process termination exceeds these selected passage guarantees.
findings.reason: These passages establish which associated processes are terminated, not the precise return/wait timing or the full TerminateProcess contract.
findings.resolution: Root supplemental exact API references and tests govern completion/cleanup confirmation; no atomic timing or single-process API guarantee is admitted from this answer.
